introResultSentence: The outcome is a negative result: in no model did either signal measurably add to the other (point estimates within $\pm4$\pp{} except one \emph{negative} one); against the official checkpoints the stage-only arm never differs significantly, and every nominally significant (uncorrected, secondary) loss is in an arm trained with boxes (pooled: up to $-10$ to $-11$\pp{} on the two world-action models), though without an action-only arm these losses cannot be attributed to the boxes. On training data the stage heads learn progress, the location heads little.
abstractResultSentence: No pre-registered contrast is supported: given one signal, adding the other changes success by at most $+3.5$\pp{} (upper 95\% bounds up to $+10.5$\pp{}), and for \awv{} adding box+location costs $8.5$\pp{} (uncorrected $p=0.03$; Holm-corrected $p=0.06$). Against the official checkpoints, all \xr{} arms gain $6.5$--$7.5$\pp{}, driven by the seen tasks, while the Awomo models lose up to $10$--$11$\pp{}, most in the arms trained with drawn boxes; but the stage-only arm also loses on \awi{}'s unseen tasks and no action-only arm was trained, so neither signal can be blamed. On training data, stage heads learn progress beyond a per-task prior and location heads little beyond a per-task constant; in a secondary test, feeding the predicted target back as a box costs \xr{} $10$\pp{} and helps neither Awomo model.
conclusionSentence: We found no evidence that the two signals are complementary, a small gain for \xr{} (F: $+7.5$\pp{}, uncorrected $p=0.049$) that we cannot attribute to either signal, and losses for the world-action models that are largest in, but not confined to, the arms trained with drawn boxes. Within our budget a stage head never measurably hurt and learned progress, whereas adding target supervision to it never helped and, for \awv{}, lowered success. Whether visual prompts present only at training time are a liability for policies that predict future frames is a hypothesis our design cannot test.
labelAuditText: Of the 103 views with a visible-target label, 26 boxes are clearly wrong (12 on a robot link or the gripper, 8 on a wrong duplicate, 3 on another object, 2 on a chair, 1 on the carried pan) and one probably; 76 to 77 (74--75\%) bound the described target, 10 of them only coarsely (supplement).
